record: Qumran Caves Expedition, March 1952 (Reed 1954; de Vaux 1953; Lefkovits 2000 pp. 1-3)
who: Ecole Biblique, ASOR and the Palestine Archaeological Museum (R. de Vaux, W. L. Reed; Cave 3 team led by H. de Contenson)
when_text: 10-29 March 1952 (camp set up 10 March, Reed p. 9; ended 29 March, Reed p. 9)
looked_at: caves in the cliffs near Kh. Qumran; Cave 3 is about 2 km north of the site
method: seven crews of one staff member and three or four Taamre workers; about 230 soundings, and work at 43 other sites (Reed pp. 9, 12); de Vaux: '230 sondages infructueux' and 37 caves or rock holes with pottery, 25 of them with Qumran-type pottery (RB 60 p. 541)
extent_depth: Ras Feshkha to Hajar el-Asbah, about 8 km of cliff; 39 caves and crevices with pottery or other objects (Reed p. 12; the Fig. 2 map numbers 40). The expedition located and searched about forty caves (New York Times, 12 Apr 1952, p. 13, from a report to A. H. Detweiler). No heavy equipment, so large boulders that might hide entrances were not moved; the larger caves got soundings only (Reed p. 9). Depth per cave not given. De Vaux 1953 gives no cave-by-cave list and no depths. His map (pl. XX, 1:20,000, 1-km grid) numbers points 1-40, of which 27 numbers are legible. Only 3Q is said to have been dug out completely: 'minutieusement fouillée dans toute son étendue' in about ten days under H. de Contenson (de Vaux p. 555).
found: Cave 3 (3Q) with the Copper Scroll (found 20 March) and other finds
documentation: Reed, BASOR 135 (1954) 8-13 (read); de Vaux, RB 60 (1953) 540-561 (read); New York Times 1 and 12 Apr 1952 (read); DJD III (1962), text volume - not accessed (the repo and Drive copies are the plates volume only)
coverage_notes: Before the scroll was read, so no entry-specific target. Reed (Fig. 2) and de Vaux (pl. XX) give maps on the Palestine grid but no cave-by-cave list or depths. De Vaux's own limits: the marl terrace was left out on purpose, which he calls 'une erreur' (4Q and 5Q were found there); some corners of the cliff were probably missed (6Q came later); one large cave 'n'a pas été entièrement fouillée' (not named); heat and illness ended the work (pp. 541-543). Points within about 0.2 km of 3Q on pl. XX: 7, 10, 4, 9, 3; only 3Q has an excavation statement (map distances measured, approximate). A numbered list may be in DJD III, text volume.
notes: Puech 2015 p. 1 and Reed p. 10 give 20 March 1952 for the find. Reed p. 12: 3Q is cave 8 on Fig. 2, about 10 m wide, 3 m deep and 2 m high before its roof fell. The first press report (Religious News Service, New York Times 1 Apr 1952) says second-revolt coins were found with the copper scrolls. Reed dates the deposit by pottery and parchment and mentions no coins; the report may confuse 3Q with Murabba'at (inference). Reed counts 39 caves with objects, de Vaux 37 (with pottery); the figures may count differently and are not reconciled. Cave 2 on pl. XX (about 2.5 km N of Kh. Qumran) is only 'un petit amas de poterie sous des blocs écroulés' (de Vaux p. 543); whether it is the 1988 juglet cave stays open.

who: R. de Vaux (Ecole Biblique) with the Jordanian Department of Antiquities
when_text: seasons attested in T02 records: L29 (1953), L83 (1954-56), L120 (1955)
looked_at: the Kh. Qumran buildings (the repo's candidate for Sekakah, entries 20-23 and nearby features)
extent_depth: not compiled here

record: Allegro's Copper Scroll Expedition, first half of April 1960 (Wright, Biblica 42, 1961, p. 1; Allegro, Search in the Desert pp. 93-94, 113-118, 'winter 1959-60'; Davies, Copper Scroll Studies 2002 pp. 28 and 35 n. 20)
who: J. M. Allegro (director); at El Mird: Canon R. de Langhe, J. Belshé, Z. Viatr, S. Jeeves, R. Izzard and G. R. H. Wright (Wright p. 1 n. 1)
when_text: 'During the first half of April 1960' (Wright p. 1); 'In the winter 1959-60 I had led a small expedition' (Allegro, Search in the Desert p. 93); '1959-60' (Davies p. 28); explorations in 1959, 1962 and 1963 (Davies p. 35 n. 20)
looked_at: 'a few of the treasure sites' (Allegro p. 93). Named: Kh. Qumran, where a detector reading at one end of the large hall led to a narrow trench (pp. 93-94); Kh. Mird (Hyrcania), where the ruins were charted, one or two graves were dug, and the square 'monument' SW of the fortress, Allegro's candidate for scroll item 2, was dug around and swept with a mine detector (pp. 113-118). Other sites are not named.
where_name: Kh. Qumran; Kh. Mird (Hyrcania) in the Buqei'a ('Vale of Achor' in Allegro); other treasure sites not named (Allegro pp. 93-94, 113-118)
method: survey for later excavation, with 'small soundings' in a few places, 'more to discover the date and purpose' of the remains than to find treasure (Allegro p. 93); detectors at Qumran; a mine detector at the Mird monument (p. 118). At the Mird monument Wright's team cleared around the base and cleared the inside 'to leave a section' (Wright p. 14); Wright mentions no detector. On the Mird summit 'No excavation was possible' (Wright p. 6, read from the page image).
extent_depth: Qumran: a narrow trench, no depth. Mird monument: square base 'slightly more than 10 metres' a side on a rock pinnacle about 300 m SW of the fortress (Palestine 1:20,000 sheet 18-12, grid 1845/1250); cleared round the base and in section; plan and section published (Wright Fig. 4, Pls. VIII-IX); clearance depth not stated (Wright pp. 2, 14-15).
found: Qumran: much pottery and animal bones, read as an oven under the plaster floor (Allegro pp. 93-94). Mird monument: a platform about 2 m wide along the NW front, 'unsuspected until clearance'; Herodian sherds in the fill; 'No chamber or deposits were located in the monument' (Wright pp. 14-15). Herodian graves already opened by Bedouin (Wright pp. 16-19). No treasure reported.
documentation: Wright, Biblica 42 (1961) 1-27 (read; plans signed 'GRHW - '60'); Allegro, Search in the Desert (W. H. Allen, 1966 reprint) pp. 93-94, 113-118 (read); Allegro, The Treasure of the Copper Scroll (1960; read) has no account of the trip; the 1964 second edition - not accessed; Albright's review, New York Times Book Review 9 Oct 1960 p. 51 (read); Reuters, New York Times 29 Dec 1961 p. 11 (read)
coverage_notes: The Mird monument is the only place in this ledger where a scroll-motivated search has a published plan and section: 'Possible references in the Copper Scroll' led the team there (Wright p. 14), and Allegro (1960 book p. 68; Search in the Desert pp. 117-118) ties it to his item 2, the sepulchral monument. The clearance found no chamber or deposit. It is still not a complete negative: Wright does not give the depth reached or say that every course was taken down, and the monument is only one candidate for the item. Allegro's mine-detector story (Search in the Desert p. 118) is not in Wright. The Qumran trench has no footprint or depth.
notes: Date: Wright, who took part, gives the first half of April 1960; Allegro's book says winter 1959-60. Either way it predates Albright's review of 9 Oct 1960, which calls the hunt unsuccessful. Wikipedia's 1962 (citing VanderKam 2010 pp. 92-93) matches the later Dead Sea Scrolls Fund expedition (S05), which was not a treasure dig. The Reuters report from Amman dated 28 Dec 1961 fits the Mazin season (S04) better than this one (inference). Allegro's 1960 book identifies item 1 (the fortress in the Vale of Achor) with Hyrcania/Kh. Mird and item 2 with a sepulchral monument belonging to it (pp. 64-68); in 1962-63 his architect found no room for steps on the east side (Search in the Desert pp. 115-116). The repo lists Hyrcania as possible for entries 16, 29 and 35 (research/sites/christmas_hyrcania_primary_followup_2026-09-30.md); how Allegro's item numbers map onto the repo's entries is not checked here.

record: Excavation at Mazin by Allegro, Stutchbury and de Langhe (Allegro, Search in the Desert pp. 1-16, 77-81, 146; Rasmussen et al. 2022 p. 2)
who: J. M. Allegro, H. Stutchbury and Mgr R. de Langhe, with Bethlehem workmen (Allegro pp. 1-4); de Langhe had earlier made a sounding at the gate (p. 3)
when_text: 'a small expedition in the winter of 1961' that lasted three weeks and ended on Christmas Day (Allegro pp. 1, 3, 13-16); Christmas Day 1960 per Rasmussen et al. 2022 p. 2; Allegro p. 2 counts 'thirteen years' from 1947, which points to 1960 (see notes)
looked_at: the Mazin building on the shore below the Kidron cliffs, a few miles south of Qumran, and its possible link to nearby caves (Allegro pp. 3-4, 9)
where_name: Mazin (Allegro never writes Khirbet Mazin or Qasr el-Yahud)
method: excavation: 'we dug trenches in and around the building' over three weeks (Allegro p. 4)
extent_depth: not reported
found: ruins 'probably dating from the time of Herod the Great' (Allegro p. 4); no objects listed. A high-water mark on the gateway is discussed (p. 80).
documentation: Allegro, Search in the Desert pp. 1-16 (read in full, owner's PDF); no plan or section published there; Allegro archives (not accessed)
coverage_notes: No scroll entry is assigned to Mazin in the repo, and Allegro links none: he presents the dig as a study of the building and of nearby habitation, not a treasure search (pp. 3-4). Not dug in the Fund expedition, when Mazin was only a camp (p. 146).
notes: Date conflict, kept open: Allegro's 'winter of 1961' against his 'thirteen years previously' from 1947 (p. 2) and Rasmussen's Christmas Day 1960. INFERENCE: Allegro says the Fund expedition came twelve months after the Mazin season (p. 162), and the only year he gives is the film broadcast of 17 April 1963 (p. 164); reading the Mazin season as December 1961 makes the Reuters report of 28 Dec 1961, citing the Department of Antiquities, the report of this dig, and fits Davies's 1962 for the Fund expedition. Not resolved.

record: Christmas Cave: first sounding (Mazin season) and the Dead Sea Scrolls Fund excavation (Allegro, Search in the Desert pp. 9-16, 57-59, 75-85, 121-131, 158; Rasmussen et al. 2022 p. 2)
who: J. M. Allegro, H. Stutchbury and the British Dead Sea Scrolls Fund, under licence from Jordan's Department of Antiquities; the excavation was supervised by Douglas Miller with Salim's workmen, with an inspector of the Department present (Allegro pp. 50, 83, 121)
when_text: found on Christmas Day at the end of the Mazin season (Allegro pp. 11-16; 1960 per Rasmussen, 'winter of 1961' per Allegro p. 3); Fund expedition from mid-November to January, year not given (Allegro pp. 37, 158), probably 1962-63 (inference: film broadcast 17 April 1963, p. 164); Rasmussen: seasons Dec 1961-Jan 1962 and Dec 1962-Jan 1963
looked_at: Christmas Cave, lower Nahal Kidron (Wadi en-Nar), near the top of the SW bank
coords: NIG 239887/621095 (Rasmussen p. 2) = OIG 189887/121095 (Porat et al. 2009 p. 31); WGS84 31.68216, 35.41991 (repo conversion)
method: first visit: a small test trench at the back of the main chamber, stopped for lack of light (Allegro pp. 13-14). Fund expedition: excavation of the lower cave by electric light, kept on purpose to the Roman upper levels (p. 121); the upper chambers sampled (p. 122); during a generator failure the workmen searched the gorge sides in small groups and cleared one Byzantine cave in three days (pp. 130-131)
extent_depth: main chamber 'about six yards square' (Allegro p. 13); excavation stopped at the Roman floor, above a twig layer and chalcolithic sherds (p. 121); no plan or section
found: first trench: Roman pottery, cloth, leather, a bone needle, a flint blade and a coin of Simon (Allegro pp. 13-14). Fund expedition: cloth, a leather pouch, a rush mat, cooking pots, date and olive stones (p. 122); Byzantine pottery, a later jar and part of a sword hilt in the upper chambers (p. 122); three lamps from the gorge cave (p. 131). Rasmussen adds a Bar Kokhba year-2 coin and small pieces of a Greek papyrus.
documentation: Allegro, Search in the Desert (read in full, owner's PDF); never published as a report; Allegro archives (not accessed)
coverage_notes: Allegro's work disturbed the cave and left spoil and sorting areas outside (Porat et al. 2009 pp. 36-37, via repo). No trench plan recovered (repo provenance note). The chalcolithic levels were left (Allegro p. 121). Allegro gives no scroll motive for this dig; he says only that the scroll names the Kidron (p. 94).
notes: Rasmussen: the team hoped for more scrolls. The SDU news item (3 Nov 2022) suggests a gold-treasure motive; that is a journalist's speculation, not a documented aim, and Allegro's book does not support it. Other Fund-expedition work (not separate rows here): a cliff cave near Mazin cleared to a chalcolithic level (pp. 78-79, 123); the cliffs behind and north of the Ain Feshkha camp searched (p. 99); two caves next to Cave 11 opened, the second dug to a chalcolithic level, its lower storey left unexplored (pp. 155-162); Kh. Mird inspected, its courtyard vault entered and measured (pp. 111-120).

record: R. J. Bull, Tell er-Ras excavations on Mount Gerizim (Bull and Wright 1965; Bull 1968; Lefkovits 2000 pp. 411-412)
who: R. J. Bull (with G. E. Wright)
when_text: surface survey 1962; probe of two to three weeks in summer 1964; six-week season from 31 May 1966; another season planned from 3 June 1968
looked_at: Tell er-Ras, the northern peak of Mount Gerizim
method: 1964: an exploratory east-west trench across the summit, then probes; 1966: rectangular plots along the axes of Building A, out to the enclosure walls (Field XII); probes for the stairway on the north slope
extent_depth: trenches reached bedrock beside Building B on the south (about 25 feet of masonry) and about 17 feet of fill inside the north enclosure wall (Bull 1968 pp. 66, 68). The fosse south of the mound is not reported as excavated.
found: Hadrian's temple (Building A) on an older Building B with mostly Hellenistic pottery; an enclosure wall; rock-cut steps in six places on the north slope; six cisterns against the north enclosure wall (I, II and VI excavated, silt with coins of AD 285-363). Bull asked whether the fosse south of the mound is the scroll's upper fosse (Bull 1968 p. 59).
documentation: Bull and Wright, HTR 58 (1965) 234-237 (read); Bull, BA 31 (1968) 58-72 (read)
coverage_notes: Bull's trench was an archaeological probe for the Hadrianic temple, not a search for the scroll's deposit. The fosse is an ancient east-west cut on the south side of the mound; Bull raised the scroll link as a question that will require further examination (Bull 1968 p. 59). No report describes digging in the fosse or under steps beside it. The steps found are on the north slope. So the scroll's place in entry 57 was not searched.
notes: Lefkovits p. 412 also proposes a 'Pool of Gerizim' reading at another entry. Bull and Wright (p. 236 n. 7) cite Milik's DJD III p. 298 reading of the Gerizim entry (his item 61).

record: Juglet of oil found in Cave 13 near Qumran, 1988 (Patrich and Arubas 1989)
who: J. Patrich (director) with B. Arubas and B. Agur; work carried out by members of Vendyl Jones's Institute for Judaic-Christian Research (Patrich and Arubas p. 43 n. 1)
when_text: February to April 1988, four caves; Cave 13 dug for seven days (pp. 43-44)
looked_at: Cave 13 of Patrich's 1984-85 survey: about 2.8 km north of Kh. Qumran and about 150 m west of the Qalia-Almog track; faces east; opening 5.5 m wide, 1.8 m high; 4 m deep, 12.5 m north-south (p. 43). Perhaps cave 2 of the 1952 survey (p. 44 n. 3).
method: excavation; northern part around a fallen boulder, a strip along the walls of the southern part and a central east-west probe trench to bedrock; all soil sieved and checked with a metal detector (pp. 45, 48)
extent_depth: bedrock at 0.2-1 m in the south; pits A and B north of the boulder followed cracks to about 2.5 m and were stopped as unsafe (p. 48)
found: Chalcolithic, Iron II and first-century pottery; the juglet, wrapped in palm fibre, in Pit B about 1 m below the surface (p. 49); a non-olive plant oil, perhaps balsam (pp. 50-59)
documentation: Patrich and Arubas, IEJ 39 (1989) 43-59, plan and section Fig. 2 (read); New York Times, 16 Feb 1989 p. A1 (read in full through ProQuest)
coverage_notes: The excavators' report is EVIDENCE with a plan, section, sieving and metal detection; Jones's identification of the oil as the Temple anointing oil is a CLAIM. The kind and result codes are left as frozen; the report would support EVIDENCE and other_finds. Distance from 3Q: Browning's sketch map (p. 76) puts the cave about 0.2 km north of 3Q; Reed's Fig. 2 puts 1952 cave 2 about 0.5 km NNW of cave 8 (3Q); Patrich's 2.8 km against Reed's about 2 km for 3Q gives about 0.8 km. Not settled.
notes: Rabbinic tradition hides the anointing oil with the ark (catalogue C21). Earlier diggers had already disturbed the cave (p. 43). The New York Times (16 Feb 1989) says the jug was found last summer; the excavators give February-April 1988 (p. 43). It says the jug was wrapped in palm leaves in a pit three feet deep inside the cave, consistent with about 1 m in Pit B. Patrich told the paper the team, with the Institute's volunteers, searched the caves for any antiquities with no specific expectations. Jones claimed the scroll lists 23 talents of this oil (a CLAIM). No location beyond a cave at Qumran.

record: Vendyl Jones's 1992 dig at the 'North Entrance to the Cave of the Column' (Browning 1996; Amar 1998; Lindell 2026; Deseret News 1992)
who: Vendyl Jones and US volunteers; M. Antelman (chemist)
when_text: arrived end of March 1992; red material reported 12 April; dig stopped by the Antiquities Authority on 18 May
looked_at: a smaller cave slightly north of the Cave of the Column, at about the same level, found in the 1989 season; chosen from a new reading of 3Q15 VI 3-5 (Browning p. 77)
method: excavation without a licence or supervising archaeologist (Lindell)
extent_depth: at the mouth: a rock-covered ramp of debris over a rock-lined pit ending on bedrock, with a lens of red material (Browning p. 77). Jones reports a dry-laid dolomite 'silo' on bedrock with 30-50 cm of red material (Amar p. 2). No section drawing exists (Amar p. 1).
found: a reddish-brown material in a 'hidden silo in the bedrock', claimed as Temple incense; salt chips and ash nearby
documentation: Browning, BA 59 (1996) 74-89 (read); Amar, DSD 5 (1998) 1-15 (read); press (Deseret News 25 June 1992); Jones, Qumran Excavations, Cave of the Column Complex & Environs (1995) - not accessed
coverage_notes: No plan or area published. The Antiquities Authority moved to stop the dig two days after the 8 May press conference, for lack of a permit (Browning p. 77). Amar reads the material as lye made at Qumran; no other participant confirmed Jones's coin or the salt in place (Amar p. 3).
notes: Date conflict: press conference 30 April (Lindell) or 8 May (Deseret; Browning p. 77). Deseret calls it Jones's seventh try.

looked_at: caves along the eastern cliffs from Wadi ed-Daliyeh to Nahal Deragot
extent_depth: about 650 caves and sites surveyed and 70 excavated (EJ)
found: finds from the Neolithic to the Ottoman period, many from the Bar Kokhba period
documentation: Atiqot 41, parts 1 (Hebrew) and 2 (English), 2002, Regions I-XV
coverage_notes: The stated goal was new scrolls. The Hebrew issue has no discussion of the Copper Scroll (repo sources.md). Region rows S20-S25 give what the repo has read.
notes: EJ notes the timing (the first Oslo Accords) was criticised.

record: 1993 survey, Regions IV and VI, Jebel Abu Saraj cliffs (Sion; Feig on IV/11), Atiqot 41 Hebrew pp. 43-90
who: O. Sion; N. Feig (IV/11)
looked_at: caves of the Jebel Abu Saraj cliff, including IV/11 'Cave of the Pillar' and IV/17 (two openings and a pillar)
coords: IV/11 site centre 190300/144150 (Greenberg-Keinan rec. 292, via repo)
extent_depth: IV/11: upper fill 60-80 cm above the Iron Age surface held the coins (Feig p. 89)
found: IV/11: Iron Age and Hellenistic/Roman material; five coins in the upper fill (two Hasmonean, two Elagabalus, one unidentified)
documentation: Atiqot 41 part 1 (Hebrew), Sion pp. 43ff, 61-64; Feig pp. 85-90
coverage_notes: IV/11 and IV/17 are the repo's entry-25 comparisons (R02). No northern-threshold datum, so the three-cubit target is not covered.
notes: Nearest places_v1 id is ain_duk; no exact id for the Abu Saraj cliff.

record: 1993 survey, Region V, Jebel Quruntul cliff (Aronshtam; Eisenberg on V/49), Atiqot 41 Hebrew pp. 91-121
who: Aronshtam; E. Eisenberg (V/49)
when_text: V/49 excavated November-December 1993 (licence L-604)
looked_at: about 650 m of the Jebel Quruntul cliff from Wadi Abu Saraj to Wadi Halq er-Rummana; caves V/1-V/69
coords: V/49 about 190400/143690 (read from Map IV-VI; schematic)
extent_depth: V/49: bedrock reached in the western hall L8 (Eisenberg p. 109)
found: V/49: Chalcolithic assemblage; Second Temple pottery (1st c. BCE to the Great Revolt)
documentation: Atiqot 41 part 1 (Hebrew) pp. 91-121
coverage_notes: V/49 and V/48 are the repo's entry-17 cave-pair lead. Map positions are schematic (50 to more than 300 m errors).

record: 1993 survey, Region VII, eastern escarpment of Jebel Quruntul (Abeles), Atiqot 41 Hebrew pp. 123-137
who: Abeles
when_text: 1993 (survey licence L-588.3; VII/1 L-611; VII/3 L-624)
looked_at: 31 caves surveyed, 16 described, on the cliff facing Jericho
method: survey; excavation of VII/1 and VII/3
extent_depth: not compiled
found: VII/3: Roman sherds, a coin of Valerius Gratus, a Nabataean coin, probable armour scales
documentation: Atiqot 41 part 1 (Hebrew) pp. 123-137
coverage_notes: The Dok summit fortress, its aqueduct and cisterns are not covered by this report, so entry 31's targets are not covered.

record: 1993 survey, Region XI, escarpment above Kh. Qumran (Baruch, Mazor and Sandhaus), Atiqot 41 Hebrew pp. 187-198
who: Baruch, Mazor and Sandhaus
looked_at: 1.4 km of the fault escarpment from the Jaufat Zabin stream south to Nahal Qumran; caves XI/1-22
extent_depth: not compiled
found: mostly 1st c. BCE-1st c. CE pottery; XI/22 an undated enclosure with a central pit
documentation: Atiqot 41 part 1 (Hebrew) pp. 187-198
coverage_notes: Kh. Qumran, its aqueduct and the Nahal Qumran dam are not drawn or discussed, so entries 20-23's built features are not covered by this report.

record: 1993 survey, Region XIV, Nahal Kidron to Nahal Deragot (Dahari), Atiqot 41 Hebrew pp. 229-247
who: U. Dahari
when_text: November 1993
looked_at: the fault escarpment from the south bank of Nahal Kidron to Nahal Deragot; also three marl caves near Kh. Qumran
extent_depth: not compiled
found: XIV/2 'Kidron (South)' site of the 1st c. CE, used to the Great Revolt; XIV/1, XIV/3, XIV/4 and the three marl caves near Qumran empty
documentation: Atiqot 41 part 1 (Hebrew) pp. 229-247
coverage_notes: Covers the lower Kidron outlet, not Mar Saba (the repo's preferred place for entry 35, 10 km upstream).
notes: The repo's phase-5 table cites Dahari for entry 35.

record: Ketef Jericho caves, 1993 (Eshel and Zissu, via T02 hoard records)
who: H. Eshel and B. Zissu (IAA 1993 operation)
looked_at: Cave of the Sandal and neighbouring caves in the Ketef Jericho cliffs west of Jericho
extent_depth: not compiled
found: 26 coins in three clusters, Vitellius to Hadrian (Bar Kokhba period)
documentation: Eshel and Zissu, ESI/HA 1995 pp. 295-298; 1999 pp. 73-77
coverage_notes: Hidden valuables of a later revolt were found in a refuge cave near Jericho; not a scroll deposit.
notes: Nearest places_v1 ids (jericho_palaces, choziba) are 2-4 km away.

record: IAA Judean Desert survey from October 2017 (T09; Times of Israel 16 March 2021)
who: IAA with the Staff Officer for Archaeology and the Heritage Ministry
when_text: from October 2017; continuing in 2021
looked_at: Judean Desert cliffs and caves
method: rappelling, drone mapping, dry sifting, metal detectors (Times of Israel)
extent_depth: about 80 km of cliffs and about 500 caves in the database by 2021 (other reports: 120 km and 400 caves); 'most of the 600-plus' caves mapped (Ganor, Times of Israel)
found: e.g. the scroll fragments announced in March 2021 (Cave of Horror)
documentation: Qadmoniot 164 (2022); IAA, New Studies in the Archaeology of the Judean Desert (2023) pp. 35-74 - not accessed
coverage_notes: Coverage of the Qumran and Jericho cliffs is not documented in accessed sources. The IAA archive request of 7 October (ACTIVE_TEST) asks for the cave records.
notes: The 2017 programme was also called 'Operation Scroll' (JNS 2017), which can be confused with 1993.

record: Qumran 'Cave 12' excavation, 2017 (JNS via Algemeiner, 8 Feb 2017)
who: O. Gutfeld and A. Ovadia (Hebrew University) with R. Price and Liberty University students
when_text: announced February 2017
looked_at: a cave in the Qumran region (position not given in the source)
extent_depth: not given
found: broken, emptied storage jars and lids; a 1950s iron pickaxe head (looting); a rolled blank parchment; leather strap, cloth
documentation: press release only in accessed sources
coverage_notes: Shows earlier undocumented looting of a Qumran cave; looters' removals are unrecorded searches.
notes: Not a Copper Scroll search.
